review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability (CS_GAME_DIR set, CS_CAPABILITIES=retail,gpu,audio); this report is derived from the recorded log plus a second production pass recorded in original-registration.json. MEASURED (identifiers, numbers, counts and digests only, no original display text, no script text): the sixteen hardpoint components T452.01's rules classify are read from the owner's weapons.zrd by read_original_component_table, read_original_weapon_records, read_original_weapon_media, read_original_ammo_declarations and read_original_weapons_provenance, then each is lowered by cs_app::ordnance::measured_ordnance_declaration and cs_app::ordnance::lower_ordnance and inserted into a real cs_sim::weapons::OrdnanceRegistry by cs_app::ordnance::register_measured_ordnance. Every value comes from a measurement: the family from the record's own keys (T452.01); the launch speed from VELOCITY, which T452-R.01 measured as metres per second along the launch direction, with Full inheritance for every record whose ACCELERATION is zero, and for a record whose ACCELERATION is non-zero the measured lateral-remainder ramp (T452-R.01): the speed scalar opens at |launcher| + 1e-4, its target is VELOCITY + |launcher|, every tick it gains dt*ACCELERATION clamped at the target, the launcher's velocity minus its launch-direction part is retained as the lateral remainder, and the recomposed velocity displaces the item by dt each step; the release delay measured as zero because T452-R.04 measured that the airframe row's refire interval delays the next release and never the current one; the per-slot stack from CLUSTER_SIZE (T452-R.03-B), cross-checked against the ammunition reader, one launch spending one unit (T452-R.02 section 5); the fuse from the record's own DETONATION_DISTANCE for a seeker, because T452-R.02 measured that the proximity path requires LOCK_ON, or from a declared DETONATION_TIME; the lost-target rule as coast-then-detonate at the end of RANGE, which T452-R.02 section 4 measured over LOCK_ON rather than over the ROCKET flag and T452-R.05 confirmed for the glidebomb wep_25; the lifetime as the record's own measured flight rule (RANGE over the flown speed, T452-R.04 section 2) evaluated at a stationary launcher and rounded up to the session's 30 Hz tick, because the runtime field is a fixed cap and the measured rule is range-bounded; the area as the record's IMPACT_PROXIMITY blast radius with the one-tick lifetime the runtime's bounded-area record needs for an instantaneous blast (T1318, T452-R.02 section 2); the damage channels from ARMOR_DAMAGE and HEALTH_DAMAGE; the marker status from BEEPER with its declared TIME (T452-R.02 section 1); and the media from the record's own FLYOUT MODEL and FIRE SOUND entry (T452-R.03-C). Two fields are designed vocabulary, not measured values, and say so: the mount key names the measured mount id (wep_05 -> weapon_mount_05) and the hardpoint kind is the project's own Underslung, because no record and no screen states where on the airframe a slot sits. The unit mass is the measured ABSENCE of a per-type term, recorded as zero: the airframe weight total adds a flat 480 weight per enabled rocket box and reads no weapon record field, so a loaded type contributes nothing to any weight total, and the flat 480/410 per box, charged per box rather than per round and in a weight unit whose conversion to kilograms is unmeasured, is kept as the named claim t452_register.limit.per_box_weight rather than converted into a kilogram figure. NOT CLAIMED: any original-run behavior (retail is read access and no agent ran the original executable); that the registered components fly as the original's do in any observable way. NOT YET EXPRESSIBLE, and therefore not registered, with the claim and the resolving task named per id: the measured silent expiry at the end of RANGE with no detonation (t452_register.limit.silent_expiry, task T452-REG-SILENT-EXPIRY, wep_12, wep_13, wep_26). A record with no declared FIRE SOUND (wep_26) is a measured silence the media record expresses as no sound, so it is not a blocker, and no retail hardpoint record lacks a FLYOUT MODEL (accept_t452_register_retail_every_hardpoint_record_declares_a_flyout_model). Nothing was defaulted to make an id register, and every measured value the runtime vocabulary cannot yet express for a declared id — the kept claims and the blockers — is listed in this report's `unknowns` with the record it sits on and the task that resolves it. The claim is implemented: a code and test pass awards nothing above that, and no agent review replaces the owner's human approval. Validated structurally with tools/validate_evidence.py - not with --require-pass, because the report's `unknowns` list carries every value this task could not express: the list is derived, not typed, from the registration report's own claims and blockers.
